model.title: State-Based Education Loan Awareness Act
model.meta: Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee · Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-AK)

summary.text: The bill would amend the Higher Education Act to add a definition of state-based education loan programs, meaning loans offered by state agencies, state authorities, or nonprofit organizations that are not funded, insured, or guaranteed by the federal government, that are approved under state law, and that offer interest rates and fees at least as favorable as federal Direct PLUS loans. Under the bill, colleges would be allowed to make arrangements or agreements about these state-based loans, and such loans would only be offered to borrowers who have been advised by their institution to first use their federal student loan eligibility before taking a private education loan, and who have been told about the rates, fees, and benefits of federal loans. The bill would also require the Comptroller General of the United States to submit a report to Congress within two years of enactment on trends among student loan borrowers, including how borrowing has changed after recent federal student loan changes, how much students borrow from federal, state-based, institutional, and private loans, the availability and interest rates of these loan types, and outcomes such as repayment, delinquency, and default rates.
